title: Landscaping PPC management for the jobs you want to win
html:
Paid search built around your crews, coverage and project mix

Wonderweb Studio plans and manages landscaping Google Ads campaigns around the work your business wants to discuss. We connect service-specific searches, relevant landing pages and inquiry tracking so you can judge the campaign by suitable opportunities, not just clicks.

Weekly lawn care, a patio installation and a commercial grounds contract have different economics and sales cycles. Putting all three into one message makes it harder to understand which work the budget is attracting. We start with your priorities, service territory, seasonality and capacity, then agree a campaign scope.

We work remotely with U.S. landscaping businesses. You keep the service knowledge and sales relationship; we handle the agreed campaign, page and measurement work with a clear review process.

Separate recurring maintenance from installation projects

The campaign structure should follow how your customers buy. These are planning examples; the final groups depend on the services you offer and the data available.

Maintenance and lawn-care inquiries

A maintenance search may need clear coverage, the type of property accepted and an explanation of recurring service. Route density and crew availability matter. The inquiry path should make it easy to identify an address and service need without promising availability the team cannot deliver.

Landscape design, hardscaping and installations

An installation prospect needs more project context: the work you undertake, relevant examples, the consultation process and broad timing. We match the message to the accepted scope rather than sending every patio or planting search to a generic lawn-care page.

Commercial grounds contracts

Property managers may compare providers, request site visits or plan a future contract. Separate their inquiry requirements from a residential estimate. Qualification can include property type, location, scope and the person responsible for selecting a vendor.

What our landscaping PPC management covers

The proposal defines the work included in your account. A focused Google Ads scope can include the following:

  • Campaign and keyword planning around selected services and accepted geography.
  • Ad copy and search-term review, with changes explained in the review process.
  • Location, schedule and budget checks against actual coverage and response capacity.
  • A review of the relevant landing page and its mobile inquiry path.
  • Conversion setup or verification for the agreed calls and forms.
  • Lead-quality reporting using the outcomes your team records.

Reduce irrelevant clicks without blocking good projects

Search-term review begins with the business brief. Employment searches, equipment sales and DIY queries may be irrelevant to a contractor selling installation or maintenance. But exclusions must reflect context: a phrase about landscape design could be valuable even when the eventual project is not described precisely.

We review the terms and available lead feedback before making broad exclusions. Negative keywords are a control to maintain, not a one-time list that guarantees zero wasted spend. Read our search-term review guide for the practical decision process.

Location settings also need review. Travel distance, accepted ZIP codes and project size may influence whether an inquiry fits. Google describes location targeting as a best-effort system, so we compare the settings with actual lead locations rather than treating a radius as a perfect fence.

Give each prospect a page that answers the next question

A landing page should help a prospective customer understand the service and request the appropriate next step. It does not need to invent urgency or hide the conditions of an estimate.

Visitor wantsUseful page contentAppropriate next step
Recurring maintenanceProperty types, coverage, service scope and genuine availabilityRequest a maintenance assessment
Patio or landscape installationRelevant project photos, scope, process and planning considerationsDiscuss the project or arrange an estimate
Commercial grounds careAccepted properties, responsibilities and contract-review processRequest a site or scope conversation

Track qualified inquiries, estimates and booked work separately

A submitted form is an inquiry. A contactable prospect with an accepted service need and location is a qualified inquiry. An estimate arranged, a proposal sent and a job accepted are later outcomes. Keeping these stages separate makes the reporting more useful to the person making budget decisions.

We agree on those definitions before evaluating performance. If forms increase but most requests are outside the territory, the campaign is not doing the job you need. If inquiries are suitable but calls go unanswered, the response process also needs attention.

We can configure the agreed measurement and reporting using the tools in your scope. Your team supplies the estimate and job outcomes. Custom CRM integrations and tracking subscriptions are itemized separately. See lead tracking beyond the form.

Set a budget around capacity and job economics

There is no single ad budget that fits every landscaping company. A seasonal maintenance route and a high-value design-build project justify different tests. We review the accepted services, market, response capacity and available account history before recommending a starting approach.

An illustrative calculation: if an accepted job contributes $2,000 before marketing and one in five qualified inquiries becomes a job, the contribution per qualified inquiry is $400 before management fees and other acquisition costs. Those are example assumptions, not a forecast or a recommended bid. Replace them with your own margins and close rate before using the calculation.

Ad spend is paid separately from management. New pages, creative, subscriptions and integrations are additional only when included in the agreed scope. Review Wonderweb pricing and the Google Ads service to compare the current options.

A clear process from account review to ongoing decisions

We begin by reviewing the account, landing pages, service mix and conversion setup. Before launch or a major change, you approve the message and scope; we verify that the inquiry path works and that someone owns the follow-up.

Build the first useful test

We choose a focused set of services and locations, prepare the agreed ads and page work, and document the initial budget and measurement. Approval, account eligibility and asset readiness affect when the campaign can start.

Use the review to make a decision

The ongoing review looks at search terms, costs and inquiry quality together. We explain which services or locations need adjustment and whether the next step is a page change, a targeting change or more reliable sales feedback. Spend increases should follow a business reason, not an automatic schedule.

Our lead guarantee for eligible campaigns

If your eligible paid campaign misses its written qualified-lead target in its first 90 days, we provide 30 additional days of campaign management at no management fee. Your advertising spend remains separate.

Available for paid campaigns whose signed proposal includes this guarantee, a qualified-lead target and the agreed media budget before launch. The 90-day period begins when the campaign launches with working tracking.

A qualified lead is a genuine, new inquiry that matches the services and service area agreed in your proposal and includes usable contact information. Duplicate inquiries, spam, vendors and job seekers do not count. Any additional qualification criteria are agreed before launch.

You maintain the agreed advertising budget, provide required access and timely approvals, keep conversion tracking working and follow the response and lead-recording process in your proposal. The campaign and lead records must be available for the 90-day review.

If those conditions are met and the target is missed, the remedy is one additional 30-day management period for the covered campaign at no management fee. Media spend, third-party subscriptions and other services remain payable. This is a management-fee waiver, not an advertising refund or a promise of sales, revenue, rankings or platform approval.

Primary references

  • Google Ads: location targeting and its limits
  • Google Ads: eligibility and placement depend on Ad Rank
